editorial:
Imagine a weird alien landing on Earth that doesn't want to talk or take over the government, but just wants to eat electricity. You get a fun, cheesy ride as this creature starts small but grows into a giant monster by draining power grids. It feels like those old-school creature features where the stakes get higher every minute. You will follow a group of worried officials and scientists who are scrambling to stop the beast before it hits a nuclear power plant and causes a total meltdown. The vibe is very much a 90s TV movie, which means it has a lot of charm and some goofy moments that make it a blast to watch with friends.

What really works here is the tension as the monster slithers across the country. While the special effects are a bit dated, they actually add to the campy fun of the whole experience. The pacing stays quick, though some of the dialogue feels a bit stiff. If you love monster movies that don't take themselves too seriously, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older title, you might want to look for a digital rental on Apple TV or see if you can find a restored version to add to your physical collection for a cozy movie night.
endingExplained: The movie reaches a climax when the giant alien finally hits the nuclear power plant. The heroes realize they cannot kill it with normal weapons, so they use its own hunger against it. They trick the creature into absorbing a massive, unstable surge of nuclear energy. Instead of making the alien stronger, the overload causes the creature to basically blow itself up from the inside. The threat is gone, and the town is saved from a meltdown.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school monster movies and 90s nostalgia.
